minutes.headline: School Committee approved a one-year paraprofessional MOA and the FY22-31 school capital plan, with one abstention on the MOA.
minutes.summary: After an executive session on union negotiations, the committee heard a Title I literacy report and a COVID-19 metrics update. It approved a one-year paraprofessional agreement, accepted a PTO donation, and approved the school capital plan to take to the Capital Planning Committee. Committee reports and adjournment followed.

A member, in the public comment slot, praised two juniors who held homemade signs on election day and urged civic involvement.

budget_items.what_was_said: Title I allocations have trended downward over three years; the funding is federal and based on low-income census counts.
The one-year MOA has zero pay increase, a small adjustment for two paraprofessionals and a one-time payment to fourteen at the top step.
The MOA cost is to come from the salary reserve fund, which still has money.
PTO donation to Turkey Hill, the second half of an award from the prior school year.
Top FY22 capital priority; designer funding was received in FY21 and the designer will refine the estimate.
Second priority; goes to the special town meeting on November 17th and returns to the plan if not approved.
Third priority covering deteriorating concrete sills and failing fascia membranes from 1969.
Boilers in FY26 and large Turkey Hill projects in later years, possibly with Green Communities or MSBA help.
Finance Committee liaison reported the town manager said CARES Act funds would cover the IT needs.
Moving some retirees into Medicare should reduce premium increases; to be watched for next year's budget.

transfers.description: MOA cost funded from the salary reserve fund

decisions.decision: The open paraprofessional positions will not be posted for now; they will serve as floating support and substitute cover, so the permission-to-post item was passed over.
The capital plan will be taken to the Capital Planning Committee next Tuesday by the facilities director and superintendent.
October 7 minutes were not in the packet, so approval was not taken up.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the FY22-31 school capital plan as presented, 5-0 by roll call, to take to the Capital Planning Committee.
The committee approved a one-year paraprofessional agreement 4-0 with one abstention; the cost is to come from the salary reserve fund.
The committee accepted a PTO donation for Turkey Hill, 5-0 by roll call.
The open paraprofessional positions will not be posted for now; they will serve as floating support and substitute cover.
The committee heard a Title I literacy report, in which Title I allocations were described as trending down over three years, and a COVID-19 metrics update.

why_it_matters: The capital plan sets the order in which school building work, such as primary school air conditioning, Turkey Hill repairs and later boilers, goes to town bodies that decide what is funded, so it shapes future capital requests that can reach tax bills.
The paraprofessional agreement is paid from an existing salary reserve rather than a new line, and falling federal Title I funding is a pressure that local budgets may be asked to absorb.
watch_next: The facilities director and superintendent take the capital plan to the Capital Planning Committee the following Tuesday.
The special town meeting on November 17 takes up the Turkey Hill administration cooling item, which returns to the capital plan if not approved.
